subject: german
title: Schlink: Der Vorleser
welcome_lead: Bernhard Schlink's Der Vorleser (1995) examines guilt, generations, and Holocaust memory.
meta_desc: German HL Literature: Schlink, Der Vorleser, Holocaust memory.
final_note: Generations meet in language — Schlink writes their encounter.

concepts.def: Older woman, secret former concentration camp guard.
Coming to terms with the (Nazi) past.

walkthroughs.body_html: 15-year-old Michael has an affair with 36-year-old Hanna in 1958. Years later, as a law student, he sees her on trial for Nazi war crimes.
The novel asks how the post-war generation should reckon with parents' complicity. The literal illiteracy of Hanna is a metaphor for moral evasion.
Praised and criticised: some argue Schlink humanises perpetrators; others see ethical insight. Reading both views sharpens analysis.
